title: How baby talk gives infant brains a boost

sentences.en: A The typical way of talking to a baby 一 high-pitched, exaggerated and repetitious 一 is a source of fascination for linguists who hope to understand how 'baby talk’ impacts on learning.
sentences.zh: A 与婴儿说话的典型方式——高调、夸张和重复——是语言学家们着迷的源泉,他们希望了解“婴儿语”如何影响学习。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Most babies start developing their hearing while still in the womb, prompting some hopeful parents to play classical music to their pregnant bellies.
sentences.zh: 大多数婴儿在子宫内就开始发展听力,这促使一些充满希望的父母向怀孕的肚子播放古典音乐。

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 分词结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: Some research even suggests that infants are listening to adult speech as early as 10 weeks before being born, gathering the basic building blocks of their family's native tongue.
sentences.zh: 一些研究甚至表明,婴儿早在出生前 10 周就开始听成人讲话,积累家庭母语的基本组成部分。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 分词结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: B Early language exposure seems to have benefits to the brain — for instance, studies suggest that babies raised in bilingual homes are better at learning how to mentally prioritize information.
sentences.zh: B 早期接触语言似乎对大脑有好处——例如,研究表明,在双语家庭长大的婴儿更擅长学习如何在心理上优先考虑信息。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: So how does the sweet if sometimes absurd sound of infantdirected speech influence a baby’s development?
sentences.zh: 那么,婴儿定向言语的甜蜜（有时甚至是荒谬的）声音是如何影响婴儿的发育的呢？

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Here are some recent studies that explore the science behind baby talk.
sentences.zh: 以下是一些最近的研究,探讨了儿语背后的科学原理。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: C Fathers don’t use baby talk as often or in the same ways as mothers - and that’s perfectly OK, according to a new study.
sentences.zh: C 一项新的研究表明,父亲使用儿语的频率和方式与母亲不同,这完全没问题。

grammar.type: 分词结构 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Mark Van Dam of Washington State University at Spokane and colleagues equipped parents with recording devices and speech-recognition software to study the way they interacted with their youngsters during a normal day.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿州立大学斯波坎分校的马克·范·达姆（Mark Van Dam）及其同事为父母配备了录音设备和语音识别软件,以研究他们在正常一天中与孩子互动的方式。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ‘We found that moms do exactly what you'd expect and what’s been described many times over,’ Van Dam explains.
sentences.zh: “我们发现妈妈们所做的正是你所期望的以及已经被多次描述过的,”范达姆解释道。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: ‘But we found that dads aren't doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: ‘但我们发现爸爸们并没有做同样的事情。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Dads didn't raise their pitch or fundamental frequency when they talked to kids.
sentences.zh: 爸爸与孩子交谈时不会提高音调或基频。

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ,Their role may be rooted in what is called the bridge hypothesis, which dates back to 1975.
sentences.zh: ,他们的作用可能源于所谓的桥梁假说,该假说可以追溯到 1975 年。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: It suggests that fathers use less familial language to provide their children with a bridge to the kind of speech they'll hear in public.
sentences.zh: 这表明父亲应该少用家庭语言,为孩子们提供一个桥梁,让他们了解他们在公共场合听到的演讲类型。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The idea is that a kid gets to practice a certain kind of speech with mom and another kind of speech with dad, so the kid then has a wider repertoire of kinds of speech to practice,' says VanDam.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是,孩子可以和妈妈一起练习某种演讲,和爸爸一起练习另一种演讲,这样孩子就可以练习更广泛的演讲类型,”VanDam 说。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: D Scientists from the University of Washington and the University of Connecticut collected thousands of 30-second conversations between parents and their babies, fitting 26 children with audio-recording vests that captured language and sound during a typical eight-hour day.
sentences.zh: D 来自华盛顿大学和康涅狄格大学的科学家收集了父母和婴儿之间数千个 30 秒的对话,为 26 名儿童穿上录音背心,记录典型的一天 8 小时内的语言和声音。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: The study found that the more baby talk parents used, the more their youngsters began to babble.
sentences.zh: 研究发现,父母使用的儿语越多,他们的孩子就越开始牙牙学语。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: And when researchers saw the same babies at age two, they found that frequent baby talk had dramatically boosted vocabulary, regardless of socioeconomic status.
sentences.zh: 当研究人员看到同样的两岁婴儿时,他们发现,无论社会经济地位如何,频繁的儿语都能极大地增加词汇量。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Those children who listened to a lot of baby talk were talking more than the babies that listened to more adult talk or standard speech,,says Nairan Ramfrez-Esparza of the University of Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格大学的奈兰·拉姆弗雷斯·埃斯帕扎 (Nairan Ramfrez-Esparza) 表示,那些听了很多儿语的孩子比听了更多成人语或标准语言的孩子说得更多。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ‘We also found that it really matters whether you use baby talk in a one-on-one context,' she adds. The more parents use baby talk one-on-one, the more babies babble, and the more they babble, the more words they produce later in life； Another study suggests that parents might want to pair their youngsters up so they can babble more with their own kind. Researchers from McGill University and Universite du Quebec a Montreal found that babies seem to like listening to each other rather than to adults - which may be why baby talk is such a universal tool among parents. They played repeating vowel sounds made by a special synthesizing device that mimicked sounds made by either an adult woman or another baby. This way, only the impact of the auditory cues was observed. The team then measured how long each type of sound held the infants’ attention.
sentences.zh: “我们还发现,在一对一的环境中是否使用儿语确实很重要,”她补充道。父母一对一使用儿语的次数越多,婴儿牙牙学语的次数就越多,而他们牙牙学语的次数越多,他们在以后的生活中说出的单词就越多；另一项研究表明,父母可能希望将自己的孩子配对,这样他们就可以与同类牙牙学语更多。麦吉尔大学和蒙特利尔魁北克大学的研究人员发现,婴儿似乎更喜欢互相倾听,而不是成年人说话——这可能就是为什么儿语成为父母普遍使用的工具的原因。他们播放由特殊合成装置发出的重复元音声音,该装置模仿成年女性或另一个婴儿发出的声音。这样,就只能观察到听觉线索的影响。然后,研究小组测量了每种类型的声音吸引婴儿注意力的时间。

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 被动语态
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: They found that the ‘infant' sounds held babies' attention nearly 40 percent longer. The baby noises also induced more reactions in the listening infants, like smiling or lip moving, which approximates sound making. The team theorizes that this attraction to other infant sounds could help launch the learning process that leads to speech. 'It may be some property of the sound that is just drawing their attention,’ says study co-author Linda Polka.
sentences.zh: 他们发现“婴儿”的声音可以让婴儿的注意力延长近 40%。婴儿的声音还会引起倾听婴儿的更多反应,例如微笑或嘴唇移动,这类似于发声。研究小组推测,这种对其他婴儿声音的吸引力可能有助于启动导致语言的学习过程。研究合著者琳达·波尔卡说：“可能是声音的某些特性引起了他们的注意。”

grammar.type: 定语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ‘Or maybe they are really interested in that particular type of sound because they are starting to focus on their own ability to make sounds.
sentences.zh: ‘或者也许他们真的对那种特定类型的声音感兴趣,因为他们开始关注自己发出声音的能力。

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: We are speculating here but it might catch their attention because they recognize it as a sound they could possibly make.1
sentences.zh: 我们在这里推测,但这可能会引起他们的注意,因为他们认为这是他们可能发出的声音。1

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: In a study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, a total of 57 babies from two slightly different age groups - seven months and eleven and a half months - were played a number of syllables from both their native language (English) and a non-native tongue (Spanish).
sentences.zh: 在《美国国家科学院院刊》上发表的一项研究中,共有 57 名来自两个略有不同年龄组（七个月和十一个半月）的婴儿播放了来自其母语（英语）和非母语（西班牙语）的多个音节。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: The infants were placed in a brainactivation scanner that recorded activity in a brain region known to guide the motor movements that produce speech.
sentences.zh: 婴儿被放置在大脑激活扫描仪中,该扫描仪记录了已知引导产生言语的运动运动的大脑区域的活动。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The results suggest that listening to baby talk prompts infant brains to start practicing their language skills.
sentences.zh: 结果表明,听儿语会促使婴儿大脑开始练习语言技能。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ‘Finding activation in motor areas of the brain when infants are simply listening is significant, because it means the baby brain is engaged in trying to talk back right from the start, and suggests that seven-month-olds’ brains are already trying to figure out how to make the right movements that will produce words,’ says co-author Patricia Kuhl.
sentences.zh: 合著者帕特里夏·库尔 (Patricia Kuhl) 表示,“在婴儿单纯倾听时发现大脑运动区域的激活非常重要,因为这意味着婴儿大脑从一开始就在试图顶嘴,这表明七个月大的大脑已经在试图弄清楚如何做出正确的动作来产生语言。”

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 状语从句
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Another interesting finding was that while the seven-month-olds responded to all speech sounds regardless of language, the brains of the older infants worked harder at the motor activations of non-native sounds compared to native sounds.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的发现是,虽然七个月大的婴儿对所有语音都有反应,无论语言如何,但与母语声音相比,较大婴儿的大脑在非母语声音的运动激活方面更加努力。

grammar.type: 状语从句 + 不定式结构
grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The study may have also uncovered a process by which babies recognize differences between their native language and other tongues.
sentences.zh: 这项研究可能还揭示了婴儿识别母语和其他语言之间差异的过程。
